description:
The SAPS scheme stands for the Scheme for Adolescent Girls. 

It was launched by the Government of India to address the nutritional and health needs of adolescent girls. 

The primary objective is to improve the nutritional status of adolescent girls aged 11 to 19 years. 

The scheme aims to empower girls through education and skill development. 

Benefits include the provision of nutritious food and health education. 

Assistance is provided in the form of take-home rations and health check-ups. 

Eligibility criteria include being an adolescent girl aged between 11 and 19 years. 

The application process typically involves registration through local Anganwadi centers. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

It operates across various states and union territories in India. 

The frequency of assistance is generally monthly. 

The scheme also focuses on life skills education and awareness about health issues. 

Additional details may include community engagement and support for out-of-school girls.
